clue.text: Flighty girl's face reported at front of carriage

indicators.note: at front of places the face piece before the word for a carriage
reported means the word for a face is to be heard spoken, and its sound written down

parts.note: phiz is an old slang word for the face, short for physiognomy
a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone describes a girl's face as she is seen at the front of a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns PHIZ, old slang for a face, into its sound; 'at front of' sets that before the carriage. 'Flighty girl's' reads as possessive, but the 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizgig is an old word for a frivolous, flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: Nice chap for whom we must be sixteen?

definitions.text: Nice chap for whom we must be sixteen?

parts.words: Nice chap for whom we must be sixteen
parts.note: a man from Nice, a city in France, says nous for 'we', and NOUS is the entry at 16 across

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French Riviera city, so the chap is from France; for him the pronoun 'we' has to be the word entered at 16 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Nice is a male citizen of France, whose language renders 'we' as nous.

clue.text: Warm and dry in centre of breezeless state

indicators.note: in places the word for warm and dry inside the central letters picked out
centre of picks the two middle letters of the ten-letter word breezeless

parts.note: to air washing is to warm and dry it, as in an airing cupboard

explanation.surface: A country with no wind, warm and dry at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle pair of a ten-letter word; 'in' sets the airing word inside. Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire was an African country, the former name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: Bold when throwing over girl of sassy disposition

parts.note: in can mean at the time of, as in 'in winter', so it stands for when

indicators.note: throwing over means the girl and the sassy word are turned round together and read backwards

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
pert means cheeky or sassy in manner

explanation.surface: A girl with a cheeky streak acts boldly as she throws something over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing over' turns the girl and the sassy word round as one run, giving TREPID; 'when' as IN is the old sense of 'at the time of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and daring, which is what bold describes.

clue.text: Booth providing two similar creatures with home

indicators.note: two means the creature word is written down twice in a row

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, and two of them are alike
in means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'

explanation.surface: A stall offering a pair of matching animals with somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booth' looks like a market stall but is John Wilkes Booth, who shot President Lincoln in 1865.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth was the man who murdered Abraham Lincoln, so he is a famous example of a killer of a leader.

clue.text: Single article creditor kept in stores? Good grief!

indicators.note: kept in means the single, article and creditor pieces are held inside the word for stores

parts.note: stows means puts away or stores
one means single
the is the definite article
CR is the abbreviation for creditor in accounts

explanation.surface: A lone item belonging to a creditor is found among the goods in storage, to someone's dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' reads as a noun but is the verb STOWS, which holds ONE + THE + CR. 'Stone the crows' is a British and Australian exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated exclamations of surprise or dismay.

clue.text: Ask woman to replace son's waterproof jacket

indicators.note: to replace means the woman's name takes the place of the letter for son in the word ask

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks a woman to stand in for her son in buying a rain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: In ASK, the S (son) gives way to NORA: A + NORA + K.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded weatherproof coat.

clue.text: Prokofiev's first trio is so curiously animated

indicators.note: curiously means the letters are put together in an odd new order
first takes only the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A trio by Prokofiev is described as unusually lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges P (from Prokofiev) with TRIO IS into SPIRITO. Spiritoso is a musical direction, which suits the composer in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritoso is the Italian musical direction for playing in a spirited, lively way.

clue.text: Music trapeze artistes use at their peril

definitions.text: trapeze artistes use at their peril

explanation.surface: Circus performers on the high bar risk everything when they go without a safety net.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as the phrase 'no net'. Read as one word it is a piece for nine players.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine instruments, and performers working without a safety net risk falling.

clue.text: Literary work left in European skiing area

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for a skiing area

parts.note: a piste is a prepared ski run

explanation.surface: A book has been abandoned on a ski run somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as abandoned, but it is the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, a kind of writing, like the books of the New Testament.

clue.text: Issue a challenge, writing article in record catalogues

indicators.note: in means the article is written into the gap between the record word and the catalogues word

parts.note: to enter something is to record it, as in a ledger
lists means catalogues or inventories
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A challenge is issued, with an item written into a register of catalogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' slots the article between the record and catalogues words; 'writing' only supports the picture. The lists were the fenced arena of a medieval joust.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter the lists is to come forward as a contender, as a knight entering the jousting arena to take on a rival.

clue.text: Scotsman attending game with neat varsity type

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a single one is an ox
on means game or willing, as in 'I'm on for it'
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot goes to a match with a tidy university student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for cattle. 'Varsity' is British slang for university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxonian is a student or graduate of Oxford University.

clue.text: Prisoner escaping from specific Greek territory

indicators.note: escaping from means the prisoner word leaves the word for specific

parts.note: concrete means specific or definite, as in 'a concrete example'
con is slang for a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A convict breaks out of a particular place in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: CONCRETE loses CON from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest of the Greek islands.

clue.text: One who treats hip with manipulation?

definitions.text: One who treats hip with manipulation?

parts.words: One who treats hip with manipulation
parts.note: reads as an anagram clue on hip, but describes a physio or osteopath who eases a sore hip joint by working it with their hands

explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulation' looks like an anagram signal on HIP, but no letters are rearranged: it is hands-on treatment of the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A physiotherapist or osteopath is a practitioner who treats injuries, often by manipulating joints.

clue.text: Government will introduce short test in month to a year

indicators.note: in means the shortened test goes inside the month word

parts.note: March is the third month

indicators.note: short means the word for test loses its last letter

parts.note: a trial is a test
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An administration plans to bring in a brief exam within a month, for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from the test word (TRIA) and 'in' sets it inside the month; 'will introduce' is only link material here.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarchy is a society or system ruled by women, a form of rule.

clue.text: Clock displaying charge I paid with hesitation

parts.note: a tax is a charge or levy
met means paid, as in 'met the bill'
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A clock shows the charge someone paid with some reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is the meter in a cab that records the fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A taximeter is the device in a cab that measures distance and time to work out the fare, and is often called the clock.

clue.text: Common sense a small number employ endlessly

parts.note: no is the short form, or small version, of number

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for employ loses its final letter

parts.note: to use something is to employ it

explanation.surface: Being sensible means putting only a few people to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final E from the employ word. NO is the usual abbreviation of number, which is why 'small' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang for practical intelligence or gumption.

clue.text: Security device Peter used, mostly working in pool

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter of the pool word is dropped

parts.note: typing is what is done in a typing pool, a room of secretaries

explanation.surface: Peter used a device for security while working in the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name but is criminal slang for a safe. 'Pool' is a typing pool, not a swimming pool; TYPING loses its G.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is a fastener with a guard over its point, designed to fasten securely.

clue.text: It's produced by people giving a hand in the pit

definitions.text: It's produced by people giving a hand in the pit

parts.words: It's produced by people giving a hand in the pit
parts.note: reads as miners helping underground, but describes theatregoers in the pit, the cheaper seats, clapping

explanation.walkthrough: 'pit' suggests a coal mine and 'giving a hand' suggests helping, but the pit is the theatre stalls and the hand is a round of clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping by an audience is the expression of approval meant by a hand given in a theatre.

clue.text: Immediately following former partner engaged by conservationists

indicators.note: engaged by means the former partner word is held inside the conservationists' letters

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A former spouse is taken on as staff by a conservation group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' tempts toward marriage with the ex, but it means held inside. The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming straight after in order or time.

clue.text: Resistant to impact of evidence after second drink

indicators.note: after means the evidence word comes behind the second and the drink

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
proof means evidence

explanation.surface: Proof of a robust constitution is that someone still stands after a second glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the evidence word behind second plus drink. Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shockproof means able to withstand knocks without damage.

clue.text: Be nineteen to little woman intervening in a row

indicators.note: intervening in means the little woman is placed within the letters for a row

parts.note: a din is a loud noise, a row
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A small woman steps in to break up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: read 19 across into it to get 'be beside'. 'Little woman' is Jo from Louisa May Alcott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin is to lie alongside or be immediately beside something.

clue.text: Creature in central Laos eating bananas in stream

indicators.note: eating means the middle of Laos swallows the stream piece
central picks out the two middle letters of the word Laos
in means the word for bananas goes inside the word for a stream

parts.note: a rill is a small stream
bananas is slang for mad

explanation.surface: In the middle of Laos, an animal eats bananas in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the bananas word inside the stream, giving RMADILL, and 'eating' has AO, the middle of the country, swallow it. 'bananas' looks like food, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an armoured burrowing animal of the Americas.

clue.text: Relish appeal over film

indicators.note: over means the appeal letters are turned round, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: SA is sex appeal
pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A tasty sauce is praised as giving a movie its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: SA reversed by 'over' gives AS, placed above PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly served with cold meats, so it is an accompaniment in the way relish is.

clue.text: Restriction Mowgli mitigated a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of the words Mowgli mitigated is used, a run across them

explanation.surface: Mowgli, the boy of The Jungle Book, relaxed a rule slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across mowgLI MITigated.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or cap placed on something.

clue.text: Married president's aids to communication

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower, so Ike's is the president's

explanation.surface: A wedded president keeps helpers to handle his communications.
explanation.walkthrough: IKE was Dwight D. Eisenhower, US president 1953 to 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikes are microphones, devices for amplifying speech.

clue.text: Heart-rending decorum regularly exhibited in mines

indicators.note: exhibited in means the picked letters are shown inside the word for mines

parts.note: pits are coal mines

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of decorum, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Moving good manners are on display at a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the alternate letters E, O, U from DECORUM, which go inside PITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Piteous means arousing pity, which a heart-rending sight does.

clue.text: Toffee-nosed southern friar going to the city

parts.note: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion
up means towards the capital or a university city, as in 'going up to London'

explanation.surface: A snooty friar from the south travels to town.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage one goes up to the capital or to Oxford and Cambridge. 'Toffee-nosed' is British slang for snobbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-up means snobbish and conceited.

clue.text: Abrupt manner of scoundrels sent back inside

indicators.note: inside means the turned word goes within the word for scoundrels

parts.note: curs are contemptible men, scoundrels

indicators.note: back means the word sent is read backwards

explanation.surface: Villains are packed off back home with a brusque attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word sent round to give TNES; 'inside' sets that within the scoundrels word.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtness is brusqueness, rudely short speech or behaviour.

clue.text: Strike leader arrested by Juan domingo — he's the third

indicators.note: arrested by means the strike leader is held inside the Argentine name

parts.note: Juan Domingo Peron was the president of Argentina

indicators.note: leader takes only the opening letter of the word Strike

explanation.surface: A union boss is detained by the Argentine leader, who is the third to be held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's the third' is grammar: 'he' is a pronoun in the third person.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'he' belongs to the third person, alongside she, it and they.
